<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915689_theRebbe_467" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915689_theRebbe_467__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Regarding our topic, the redemption of the Alter Rebbe, these three matters apply to him as a divine servant, and through them he was redeemed in peace.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And now, regarding our topic</t>
    <t s="1">(the redemption of our Rebbe, the Alter Rebbe16),</t>
    <t s="2">it is understood</t>
    <t s="3">that these three matters — pertain to the divine servant,</t>
    <t s="4">namely our Rebbe, the Alter Rebbe,</t>
    <t s="5">who was redeemed in peace.</t>
    <t s="6">And as he writes, "When I read the verse 'He redeemed in peace... I went out in peace,'"</t>
    <t s="7">he himself engaged in these three matters while he was imprisoned</t>
    <t s="8">(and therefore his reading was effective)</t>
    <t s="9">and through this he was redeemed in peace.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>It is puzzling how communal prayer was possible in prison, but the Tzemach Tzedek explains that an individual's prayer needed by the many is like communal prayer.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one must understand,</t>
    <t s="1">how was the service of communal prayer possible while he was in prison?</t>
    <t s="2">For the study of Torah, and in the manner of being engaged in it, is also applicable while in prison,</t>
    <t s="3">and also engaging in acts of kindness while in prison, as Hillel said,</t>
    <t s="4">when he would go to eat,</t>
    <t s="5">that he is going to perform kindness with the wretched and poor — that is his own body17,</t>
    <t s="6">but how could he pray with a minyan? And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="7">as explained by his holy honor, the Tzemach Tzedek18</t>
    <t s="8">(this year19</t>
    <t s="9">being the centennial year of his passing)</t>
    <t s="10">— that the prayer of an individual which the many need is like communal prayer.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Alter Rebbe explains that "here for an individual" refers to the Yechidah of the soul, and communal prayer also relates to the Yechidah, which is the innerness of Kesser.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And now, the explanation of our Rebbe, the Alter Rebbe20</t>
    <t s="1">author of the redemption and joy, on the Sages' statement21</t>
    <t s="2">"Here for an individual, there for the community,"</t>
    <t s="3">that "here for an individual" is the aspect of Yechidah in the soul.</t>
    <t s="4">And from the fact that the Gemara compares "there for the community" to the matter of "here for an individual"</t>
    <t s="5">(during the Ten Days of Repentance),</t>
    <t s="6">it is understood that also the matter of communal prayer</t>
    <t s="7">pertains to the aspect of Yechidah.</t>
    <t s="8">For in the matter of the Sefiros, it is the aspect of the innerness of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="9">as explained in the maamar</t>
    <t s="10">(section 13)</t>
    <t s="11">that communal prayer is from the aspect of the innerness of Kesser.</t>
    <t s="12">And so it is also regarding the matter of engaging in Torah</t>
    <t s="13">(the innerness of Torah)</t>
    <t s="14">and acts of kindness</t>
    <t s="15">(which is above charity)</t>
    <t s="16">that they are from the aspect of the innerness of Kesser — which in divine service is the aspect of Yechidah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
